title: Causal prefix preservation: hybrid LRU/TTL eviction with proof obligations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As continuous batching increases request concurrency, prefix-scoped KV entries (per-tenant or per-prefix context) must be evicted in a way that preserves causal correctness: a cache hit must never return stale KV state that would break model generation determinism for an in-flight request. Existing LRU/TTL hybrids at Redwood have handled throughput and cost but lack a concise invariant and deployable proof obligations for correctness under concurrent batch execution and prefix migration.

Goal: Design and implement a hybrid eviction policy that: 1) combines LRU recency and TTL age, 2) is prefix-aware (supports pinning/prefix groups), 3) integrates with continuous batching (handles inflight KV references and batched KV pin/unpin operations), and 4) provides machine-checkable correctness obligations and a testing harness to validate invariants under fuzzed scheduling.

Proposal summary: Introduce "epoch watermarks" per-KV-shard and per-prefix plus a lightweight "causal handle" attached to inflight batch contexts. Eviction candidates are selected by a triage score: score = lambda1 * normalizedLRU + lambda2 * normalizedTTL + lambda3 * prefixAffinityPenalty. Before eviction, candidate entries enter a two-phase demotion: (A) mark-as-demoting with epoch stamp E_demote, (B) grace period where inflight causal handles with epoch <= E_demote are allowed to complete reading. If any inflight handle references the entry, eviction is deferred and the slot is re-prioritized. After the window, the entry becomes evictable and can be reclaimed.

Key invariants (to be enforced and tested):
- Causal preservation invariant: If request R started with causal_epoch <= entry.epoch, R must never observe the entry after it has been reclaimed. (This implies demote must wait for all handles with epoch <= demote epoch.)
- Prefix consistency invariant: All entries pinned by a prefix-group must not be evicted while any active prefix-scope rollout or migration references them.
- Memory safety invariant: GPU memory reclamation happens only after host-visible invalidation and explicit KV-slot fence; no device pointer is reused until all outstanding kernels referencing it complete.

Correctness obligations / proof sketch:
1) Model the system as a partial order of events: handle-alloc, read, demote-mark(E), reclaim(E). Show demote-mark increases epoch monotically per shard/prefix.
2) Prove by contradiction: assume a read observes reclaimed entry; then there exists a read R with handle epoch h <= E_demote but reclamation happened before R finished. Because reclamation checks outstanding handles by epoch, contradiction.
3) Reduce device-level safety to host fence ordering: reclaim performs device fence plus host write to a reclaimed ledger entry; any kernel capturing the old pointer must be submitted before the fence. This aligns driver semantics across NVIDIA/AMD.

Implementation plan:
- Runtime: add per-shard epoch counter and per-prefix pinned_epoch. Integrate epoch stamping into batching front-end where each batch is assigned a causal_epoch on dequeue.
- Eviction path: scoring function + mark-demote + grace timer tied to inflight-handle counter (or epoch-based wait). Avoid global sleeps: use wait-free counters and notify on handle completion.
- Fallback: if grace window exceeds threshold for memory pressure, escalate to cooperative GC: schedule priority draining of inflight contexts by backpressure (returning 429-like error to oldest clients) or trigger opportunistic model fallback (lower KV reliance).
- Tests: unit tests for epoch monotonicity, integration fuzz tests under synthetic continuous-batching workloads, GPU mem stress test that forces reclamation while many small kernels are active; property-based tests to assert causal preservation invariant across random interleavings.
- Rollout: feature flag behind runtime-eviction-v2; small canary on dedicated pool with telemetry (eviction-deferrals, grace-window-distribution, reclaimed-by-prefix).

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation merges with full unit and integration tests.
- Fuzz harness demonstrates zero invariant violations in 1M scheduling permutations.
- Production canary shows <1% tail increase in latency and memory pressure reduced vs baseline under same throughput.
- Telemetry emits per-eviction-event fields: shard, prefix, pre_score, demote_epoch, deferrals, reclaim_latency_ms.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How to pick lambda weights for score: recommend adaptive learning from historical access patterns; initial conservative defaults favor prefix affinity to limit correctness risk.
- Granularity of epoch (per-batch vs per-request) — per-batch is lower overhead but coarser; recommend per-batch initially.
- Edge case: long-lived pinned prefixes blocking reclamation under extreme memory pressure — need admin-override policy.
